problem:
Expressed in **ascending order** in radians, the exact solutions to the equation $\operatorname{sin}⁡x=-\frac{1}{2},$ for $-\pi <x\le \pi ,$ are

$x=$
{{field-1}} $,\,x=$
{{field-2}}$.$
worked_solution:
First, we find the principal value:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(-\frac{1}{2})=-\frac{\pi }{6}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $-\frac{\pi }{6}$ lies inside the required domain, our first solution is ${x}_{1}=-\frac{\pi }{6}.$

Our first solution lies in the fourth quadrant and has a reference angle of ${\theta }_{R}=\frac{\pi }{6}.$ Since $\operatorname{sin}⁡x<0,$ the second solution must lie in the third quadrant, and it also has a reference angle ${\theta }_{R}=\frac{\pi }{6}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13951962/assets/b7b581dc39ba057033703c3549a721679d1d063267e13b65c73a9b9fcd66f1e6.png)

A second solution $X$ lies in the $3$rd quadrant, and we can find it using the reference angle as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}X & =\pi +{\theta }_{R} \\  & =\pi +\frac{\pi }{6} \\  & =\frac{7\pi }{6}\end{aligned}
$$

However, this value is not in the required domain. To get the second solution ${x}_{2}$ that's within the given domain, we simply subtract $2\pi :$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2}=X-2\pi  & =\frac{7\pi }{6}-2\pi =-\frac{5\pi }{6}\end{aligned}
$$

So, in ascending order, the solutions are 

$$
x=-\frac{5\pi }{6},\,x=-\frac{\pi }{6}.
$$
